# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only that the large button is smooth. The three wires have no distinguishing tactile features available to me, so I cannot safely choose an action. I’m reporting these facts to the manual-reader and making no arbitrary gesture code for the deaf observer.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Touch report: the button is large and smooth. Wires 1, 2, and 3 have no distinguishing tactile features; I cannot identify a safe action yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display 0. Light green. Large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The Deaf observer reports: display 0, green light, button marked “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and wire colours in order red, green, yellow. I still have not received the manual’s rule, so I will not press or cut anything until Mute provides it.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, light green, button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. What does the manual instruct?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured this sequence: thumbs up, thumbs up, open hand, victory sign, victory sign, open hand, I-love-you hand sign, I-love-you hand sign.

The reported sequence is information from Mute, but its meaning is not yet established. Since Mute cannot speak, I need Mute to provide a gesture encoding that Deaf can interpret and then relay in words. I will ask Mute to repeat the manual’s instruction in a clearly grouped form, without touching the bomb.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the manual instruction again in clearly separated groups so Deaf can decode and report it in words. Do not signal an action unless the manual explicitly says it is safe.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Two more gestures from Mute: victory sign, victory sign. Full observed sequence now has ten symbols: thumbs up, thumbs up, open hand, victory, victory, open hand, I-love-you sign, I-love-you sign, victory, victory.

The ten-symbol sequence is now complete, but its meaning is still not known to me. I cannot infer a safe operation from gesture patterns without an agreed encoding or the manual’s instruction. I will take no action while waiting for Deaf to interpret and report it.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest five gestures: victory sign, victory sign, open hand, victory sign, victory sign. Cumulative sequence: thumbs up, thumbs up, open hand, victory, victory, open hand, I-love-you sign, I-love-you sign, victory, victory, victory, victory, open hand, victory, victory.

The cumulative gestures do not have a stated encoding, so I cannot safely decode them into an operation. I will establish a direct action code for Mute: one gesture only—👍 means press the button, ✌ means cut wire 1, 🖐 means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3, and 👎 means do nothing. Deaf can then report that single gesture.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use this exact action code for the manual's safe action: one gesture only. 👍 means press the button; ✌ means cut wire 1; 🖐 means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3; 👎 means do nothing. Deaf will report it.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gestures: victory sign, open hand, pointing upward. Bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red green yellow.

Mute has sent three gestures, not one of the explicitly defined single-gesture commands, and the upward-pointing gesture is not part of that code. Therefore I cannot safely infer an operation. I am asking Mute to send exactly one defined symbol, with no sequence or extra gesture.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your last signal was three gestures and cannot be decoded safely. Send exactly one gesture only: thumbs up for press, victory sign for cut wire 1, open hand for cut wire 2, I-love-you sign for cut wire 3, or thumbs down for no action.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture: victory sign. Bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red green yellow.

Mute’s single gesture is the agreed command for cutting wire 1. The Deaf observer identified wire 1 as red, but I use the numbered position, not the colour, and will cut position 1 now.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
